newsitem.title: USA: Snow, mud slides leave 5 dead in U.S. Northwest.
newsitem.headline: Snow, mud slides leave 5 dead in U.S. Northwest.

text.p: At least five people were killed and more than 100,000 homes were left without power Tuesday after a late fall storm dumped rain and snow across the Pacific Northwest.
Heavy rains triggered devastating mud slides in Oregon, where four people died when the house they were in was swept down a hillside.
Up to 10 inches of heavy, wet snow fell in the Seattle area, causing hundreds of traffic accidents and closing most schools.

Betty Werblun, a spokeswoman for Puget Power, said about 75,000 of the company's 865,000 customers were without power, mostly because tree branches heavy with snow had fallen or sagged onto power lines.
She had no estimate of when power might be restored.
"Our trucks are having as much trouble as everyone else in getting where they're going," she said.
The Seattle area averages only 11 inches of snow a year.
In the Cascade Mountains east of Mount Rainier, a hunter was killed when a tree snapped under the weight of snow and came crashing down onto the motor home in which he was sleeping.

Gregory Carlson, 29, was killed instantly in the accident near Cliffdell, Washington, while two other hunters sleeping in the motor home were uninjured, said Yakima County Sheriff's spokesman Jim Hall.
In Oregon two children escaped from their home just before their parents and two acquaintances were swept to their deaths by a mudslide, said Douglas County Sheriff's Capt. Robert Stratton.
He said the wood frame home was carried more than 300 yards as the hillside gave way.
"It was literally demolished," he said. "There's nothing left but kindling."

Deputies recovered the bodies of Rick and Susan Moon, both in their 40s, and a neighbor, Sharon Marvin. A fourth victim was not identified, and Stratton did not know the ages of the children, who were staying with neighbors.

About 25,000 people remained without power in Oregon, down from 100,000 at the peak of the storm, a spokeswoman for Portland General Electric Co. said. Smaller utilities reported that thousands of additional customers were without power.
At Seattle's SeaTac International Airport many flights were delayed or canceled and some travelers were stranded, although runways remained open, said airport spokeswoman Anita Risdon.
"It definitely slowed down operations for some time," Risdon said. "Now we're pretty much back on track."
Forecasters were calling for freezing temperatures overnight with more snow possible north of Seattle.
